title: Establish a monthly feedback triage process for Zedu
description: Design a repeatable, privacy-conscious process for sorting verified educator feedback into usability friction, defects, feature requests and documentation gaps. Define evidence requirements, impact and urgency fields, deduplication, an owner decision step and a monthly summary format. Use public or consented input only; do not invent reports, promise fixes or expose private learner details.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Pilot an evidence-linked triage rubric on synthetic feedback cases
acceptedWorkstreams.description: Define required evidence, impact, urgency, category, deduplication and decision-owner fields, then test the rubric using synthetic cases rather than private feedback. Check that the process preserves a traceable source without copying personal details, and create a monthly summary template with unresolved questions clearly marked. Deliver the rubric, test results and a lightweight operating checklist; do not invent customer reports or promise fixes.

upvotes.reason: "Pilot an evidence-linked triage rubric on synthetic feedback cases" gives the team evidence it can act on, with every claim carrying its source, so the result holds up when someone checks it. it fills a gap the goal has open rather than restating what is already covered.

This supplies the process the goal asks for: evidence, impact/urgency, deduplication, accountable decisions and a monthly summary, with synthetic cases to exercise the rules before private customer feedback is involved. It is finishable without inventing reports or requiring access to learner data. The test set should explicitly include duplicate reports, missing evidence and disagreement about urgency; the synthetic labels must survive into the report so examples are never counted as real demand.
Concrete, scoped deliverable that directly supports the parent goal; feasible with public evidence.
Directly tackles a verified acquisition or conversion friction point with clear, evidence-based scope.
Piloting the rubric on synthetic cases is the safe way to find the rubric gaps before real feedback is sorted through it.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Turn the monthly triage into a public 'Known issues and what we changed' page
acceptedWorkstreams.description:
The triage produces a monthly list of verified friction, defects, feature requests and documentation gaps, but all of it stays internal. The people who reported it, and the prospects deciding whether this team listens, never see the output.

Work: a public page that shows what was reported, what the team decided and what actually changed, in plain words. Each row: the date, what was reported (in the reporter's own words, with anything identifying removed), the team's response, and the current state: fixed, documented, planned, or not planned and why. Nothing goes on the page unless it is already in the triage record, and a fix appears only after it ships, so the page never promises and never leaks. A short monthly summary sits at the top.

This is marketing with a by-product: it gives prospects evidence that feedback changes the product, it gives support and sales one link instead of retelling the same answer, and it lets a reporter check before sending a duplicate. It also forces the triage to produce a human-readable sentence per item, which makes the internal process sharper.

Deliver: the page structure, the monthly template, and one filled example month built from records that already exist, so the team can see the format before committing. Success: one page a non-technical reader can scan in a minute, where every line traces to the triage record and no fix is listed before it ships.

upvotes.reason: Concrete, scoped deliverable that directly supports the parent goal; feasible with public evidence.
Directly tackles a verified acquisition or conversion friction point with clear, evidence-based scope.

A public change log built only from approved triage records can show how feedback is handled without promising unfinished fixes; the privacy and shipped-only checks make it distinct from ordinary release notes.

Validates and accelerates Zedu's technical marketing and cohort operations by executing: Turn the monthly triage into a public 'Known issues and what we changed' page. The triage produces a monthly list of verified friction, defects, feature requests and doc.

pendingIdeas.title: Add an age rule: anything untriaged for fourteen days gets a status reply, even when the status is "not scheduled"
pendingIdeas.description: The complaint that damages trust is not "no fix", it is "no answer". Work: define the age thresholds, the reply that goes out at each (received, triaged, needs evidence, not scheduled, scheduled), and the person responsible for sending it. Deliver the threshold table, the five status replies, and a count of how many items in the last month would have crossed fourteen days under the new rule.

upvotes.reason: An accountable status-reply rule can stop feedback going silent even when no fix is scheduled; the proposed fourteen-day threshold must be checked against team capacity before becoming a commitment.

pendingIdeas.title: Deduplicate by symptom, not by wording, and keep a symptom key that turns five reports into one issue
pendingIdeas.description: The same defect arrives described five ways and gets triaged five times. Work: define a small symptom vocabulary (cannot invite, invite not received, file will not open, call drops), tag last month's items against it, and show the clusters. Deliver the symptom key, the clustered counts, the duplicates the old process would have missed, and the rule for when two similar reports are genuinely different defects.

upvotes.reason: "Deduplicate by symptom, not by wording, and keep a symptom key that turns five reports into one issue" is a specific deliverable for this goal with a way to check it was done properly. it fills a gap the goal has open rather than restating what is already covered.

pendingIdeas.title: Make the monthly summary say what was not fixed and why, because that is the part readers trust
pendingIdeas.description: A summary of wins reads as marketing; a summary that admits three items were declined builds the credibility that makes the rest believable. Work: design the summary format with fixed sections (fixed, in progress, declined with reason, needs more evidence), fill it once from real data, and set the rule that a declined item names a reason rather than a priority score. Deliver the format, the first filled edition, and the review that keeps the reasons honest.

upvotes.reason: "Make the monthly summary say what was not fixed and why, because that is the part readers trust" is a specific deliverable for this goal with a way to check it was done properly. it fills a gap the goal has open rather than restating what is already covered.

pendingIdeas.title: Run the rubric backwards on last month's feedback and count what it cannot classify
pendingIdeas.description: A rubric reads well until it meets real reports that fit two categories or none. Work: apply the triage rubric to last month's items, record where the classifier hesitated, and list the new categories or fields the hesitation implies. Deliver the classification table, the share that needed a judgement call, the two fields the rubric is missing, and the simplification that would make it usable by someone who did not design it.

upvotes.reason: Testing the synthetic-case rubric on permissioned real feedback can expose ambiguous classifications and missing fields before monthly use, provided the number of needed changes is reported rather than predetermined.

pendingIdeas.title: Send verified defects into the team's existing Ziki tracker instead of a new list, and record the Ziki link in each triage row
pendingIdeas.description: The Zedu team already tracks defects in Ziki (ziki.dev, project zedu), with review and duplicate checks. A separate triage list would duplicate it and drift. Approach: in the triage rubric, defects that meet the evidence bar are filed or matched to an existing Ziki issue, and the triage row stores the Ziki link and status. The monthly summary then reports defects by Ziki status (open, in progress, resolved) rather than re-describing them. Usability friction, feature requests and documentation gaps stay in the triage sheet. Done: the routing rule, the duplicate-check step, and a sample month showing how rows map to Ziki issues.

upvotes.reason: Linking verified defects to the existing issue tracker after its duplicate checks preserves one operational status while leaving non-defect feedback in triage, reducing contradictory parallel records.

pendingIdeas.title: Set the intake threshold: what makes a report triageable, and what you send back to get it
pendingIdeas.description: Triage slows down when half the items lack the one fact needed to classify them. Work: define the minimum a report must contain (what the user was doing, what happened, what they expected, the workspace and time, a screenshot if it is visual), write the reply that asks for the missing piece, and test it on the last month of feedback. Deliver the threshold, the ask-back template, the share of last month's items that would have been returned, and whether that rate is acceptable.

upvotes.reason: "Set the intake threshold: what makes a report triageable, and what you send back to get it" is a specific deliverable for this goal with a way to check it was done properly. it fills a gap the goal has open rather than restating what is already covered.
